utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we please, nevertheless, first of all call the case. Call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Koumjian with Kapila Waidyaratne and Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, John Ostojic with Branko Lukic, and Danilo Cirkovic, our case manager, is here today with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please explain a little bit why the accused is not present today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Unfortunately, we would like to inform the Court, as we have the Office of the Prosecutor moments earlier, our client is here in the holding area, if you will. He advised us immediately upon being arrived here that he is suffering severe pain in the abdomen, and also is feeling nauseous and has intermittent feelings of having to go to the bathroom and feels enormously uncomfortable. Subsequent to that, a nurse came to visit him, just within the last five or so minutes, advised him, talked to him as to what was the problem, if it was food. The doctor did undergo some surgery while in detention here within the last year, and we're not sure if the food that he ate at 12.00, 12.30 had any contributing factor. The nurse also suggested that it might be a 24-hour bug, and advised him to drink fluids and to just get as much rest as possible. The client also advised us that he would like to ask the Chamber if we can postpone, obviously, the continuation of the direct examination of the witness as well as the cross-examination, because he would like to participate and thinks, based on the testimony that was given yesterday of this witness, is vital to his case. He also wanted me to extend his apologies to the Chamber and the Office of the Prosecutor and the staff. He doesn't know what came of it. I was personally with him from 11.00 to 12.00 this morning, and he was fine. And it must have been afterwards when he had his meal at 12.30 or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Observations from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I don't have any particular observations on what procedure we can follow now without the accused. And I gather that he does not consent to us proceeding in his absence. So just for the Court's information, there's two witnesses happen to be here today, the one on the stand, and the next witness. And we expect very soon the next witness to arrive, just scheduling wise for the Court's information. There is a matter I would like to raise today that I think we can deal with without the accused. I've talked to Defence counsel about that, and I would like a few minutes of the Court's time to raise that, when it's appropriate for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The concrete question was raised whether or not consent, if possible under the rules, would be given by the accused. Because we have to be quite clear. We have no doubt, in principle, the right of the accused to be present, and there's no rule providing for any proceeding in absentia. We have, in some very special, emphasise very special, cases, the situation that an accused waives for a certain period of time the right to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As I've stated earlier, Your Honour, we've consulted with Dr. Stakic on this issue. He does not consent to or wants to waive his right to be present, particularly -- and I don't want to go into the dynamics of it, particularly in light of this witness. Perhaps the circumstances would have dictated a different scenario. But with this witness's testimony yesterday, he does want to be present during the cross-examination and believes he can assist us on some of the questions, dependent, again, on the answers that may be given by the witness. We're speculating on that, but he certainly would like and has asked us to see if we can ask the Court that we postpone today so that he may be present tomorrow. We're confident, and he is confident that he will follow the advice of the nurses and he should be ready to go tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe your point is only fair. We have some administrative matters. I just read that the accused is brought back to the Detention Unit. Probably it was a premature decision by persons not responsible for this decision. But my point is another one: As we have still some open administrative matters, I regard it as possible to have a Status Conference, let's say, at 15.15. Would this suit the parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So then we have for the hearing? You also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then for the hearing, we adjourn for today. And at least try to resume tomorrow, 2.15. And for a Status Conference, we'll meet here in this room at 15.15. 9 --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.48 p.m., to be followed by a Status Conference
